section_summary: This section follows U.S. and occupation policy on Japanese petroleum production, storage, distribution, shipping and refining from January 1948 through July 1949. It records disagreement over nationalizing oil production, the return of petroleum distribution to private operators, negotiations over Japanese tanker voyages to the Persian Gulf, and the eventual lifting of restrictions on Pacific coast refineries. The final information bulletin continues beyond page 134.

subfiles.title: Petroleum industry reorganization report, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Argues for a fully government financed organization to replace Imperial Oil's mixed ownership structure.
subfiles.summary: The report describes lease concentration, overstaffing, political influence, financial instability and weak exploration. It proposes dissolving the existing organization, cutting personnel, releasing unused leases and assisting independent producers.

subfiles.title: Proposed petroleum production legislation
subfiles.about: Reports objections to proposed nationalization of Japanese petroleum production.
subfiles.summary: Commerce and Government Sections oppose provisions that could restrict private Japanese or foreign exploration and production; Tokyo requests Department guidance.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese petroleum production policy
subfiles.about: States Department preference for competitive private oil development and revised mining laws.
subfiles.summary: The Department favors private development but recognizes a freely made Japanese decision for public ownership.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum concerns about the Kodan
subfiles.about: Requests an earlier end to the Petroleum Distribution Kodan and access to oil terminals.
subfiles.summary: Parker fears an extended Kodan monopoly and petroleum production nationalization will hinder Standard-Vacuum's return to Japan.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum request to recover its Japanese trade
subfiles.about: Seeks restoration of Standard-Vacuum property, management and distribution rights in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Parker argues that continued exclusion threatens prewar investments and may lead to nationalization.

subfiles.title: Re-establishment of free enterprise in petroleum marketing
subfiles.about: Proposes ending the Kodan and restoring foreign companies' facilities and distribution roles.
subfiles.summary: Parker urges termination of Kodan and Josco, return of storage assets and renewed commercial importation and distribution.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Parker's proposals
subfiles.about: Acknowledges requests to end Kodan operations and aid private acquisition of terminals.
subfiles.summary: Thorp promises departmental consideration of Parker's two proposals.

subfiles.title: Japanese tankers without Allied representatives
subfiles.about: Requests approval for Japanese tankers to call at British ports without Allied representatives aboard.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites naval staffing difficulties, added cost and satisfactory Japanese merchant marine performance. Commercial agents would handle ships' business while SCAP retained control.

subfiles.title: British approval of Japanese tanker port calls
subfiles.about: Approves Japanese tanker calls at Singapore and Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Britain raises no objection to port calls on the Persian Gulf shuttle.

subfiles.title: Request for British approval of tanker shuttle
subfiles.about: Seeks approval for Japanese tankers carrying Persian Gulf oil to call at British ports.
subfiles.summary: The proposal would free U.S. tankers and reduce dollar costs; an American officer would accompany each Japanese vessel.

subfiles.title: British approval of tanker port calls, filed copy
subfiles.about: Confirms no objection to Japanese tanker calls at Singapore or Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Filed copy of the British approval.

subfiles.title: Use of Japanese tankers on the Middle East run
subfiles.about: Suggests seeking Saudi clearance for Japanese tankers loading at Ras Tanura.
subfiles.summary: Keyes notes British clearance and asks for a cable to Jeddah.

subfiles.title: Cable requesting tanker clearance
subfiles.about: Initiates a request for clearance concerning Japanese tanker calls.
subfiles.summary: The telegram body is unreadable in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Saudi inquiry about tanker status
subfiles.about: Reports a Saudi question whether the Japanese tankers are civilian or military.
subfiles.summary: Childs asks the Department for clarification.

subfiles.title: Clarification of Japanese tanker status
subfiles.about: Explains that Japanese tankers are civilian owned and crewed but carry a U.S. naval supervisor.
subfiles.summary: The tankers primarily serve Japanese civilian oil needs.

subfiles.title: Question about consulting Saudi Arabia
subfiles.about: Reports concern that requesting Saudi permission could establish an unwanted precedent.
subfiles.summary: The Legation suspends action pending further instructions.

subfiles.title: Reason for Saudi tanker clearance request
subfiles.about: Explains the courtesy request for Japanese sailors to enter Saudi ports.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites the sailors' enemy alien status and wishes to avoid difficulties.

subfiles.title: Jeddah tanker clearance cable
subfiles.about: Responds to earlier telegrams on Japanese tanker clearance.
subfiles.summary: The substantive message is illegible in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Request for prompt reply on tankers
subfiles.about: Presses for a reply on Japanese tanker clearance.
subfiles.summary: The Navy is seeking an answer.

subfiles.title: Use of Japanese tankers for Middle East oil
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP tanker directive and newspaper article.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Japanese tanker sailings have begun and more vessels will become available.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1924: Japanese tankers for fuel oil
subfiles.about: Directs use of Japanese tankers to lift fuel oil from Bahrain and Ras Tanura.
subfiles.summary: The directive sets loading, receipt, reporting and interagency arrangements.

subfiles.title: 16 Japan Tankers Sailing to Persia to Bring Back Oil
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese tanker voyages for Persian Gulf fuel oil.
subfiles.summary: The article describes the first sailings and anticipated U.S. tanker savings.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of petroleum storage directives
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP directives on petroleum storage tanks.
subfiles.summary: Notes arrangements restoring some Standard-Vacuum and Rising Sun facilities.

subfiles.title: Information concerning SCAPIN 1920
subfiles.about: Explains restrictions on petroleum storage tank alterations.
subfiles.summary: SCAP seeks to preserve excess tank capacity for reparations or scrap.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1920: Petroleum Storage Tank Facilities
subfiles.about: Requires prior approval for major changes to storage tanks over 50 kiloliters.
subfiles.summary: Orders an inventory of large tanks by September 1948.

subfiles.title: Release of petroleum distribution from occupation control
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP directives on private terminal operation and tank preservation.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo reports that main terminals are to move from Kodan operation to private operators under approved service contracts.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1930: Private operation of petroleum terminals
subfiles.about: Directs transfer of main oil terminals from Kodan operation to private enterprise.
subfiles.summary: Private operators would distribute Kodan petroleum under service contracts with approved fees.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1920: Petroleum Storage Tank Facilities, second copy
subfiles.about: Restricts alterations to petroleum tanks over 50 kiloliters.
subfiles.summary: Another filed copy of the tank directive.

subfiles.title: Information concerning SCAPIN 1920, second copy
subfiles.about: Clarifies that excess oil tanks should remain available for reparations or scrap.
subfiles.summary: Another filed copy of the explanatory memorandum.

subfiles.title: Reply to Charles van Bergen
subfiles.about: Responds to an inquiry about Japan.
subfiles.summary: Only fragments of the reply survive in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Request to withdraw refinery policy letter
subfiles.about: Requests return without action of a December 1948 letter on Japanese refinery policy.
subfiles.summary: Loomis cites changed circumstances.

subfiles.title: Return of Loomis's refinery policy letter
subfiles.about: Returns Loomis's December 1948 letter as requested.
subfiles.summary: The original inquiry about reactivating Japanese refineries is returned without action.

subfiles.title: Petroleum situation in the Far East
subfiles.about: Records Asiatic Petroleum's views on Japan's distribution business and Korea's Kosco lease.
subfiles.summary: Read reports property recovery and expected expansion of private distribution after Kodan dissolution. Duncan raises unresolved Korean lease negotiations.

subfiles.title: Removal of Allied representatives from tankers
subfiles.about: Reports requests for British and Saudi approval to remove Allied representatives from Japanese tankers.
subfiles.summary: The change responds to a SCAP request.

subfiles.title: Saudi clearance for unaccompanied tankers
subfiles.about: Seeks Saudi approval for Japanese tankers without U.S. representatives aboard.
subfiles.summary: Vessels would remain under the SCAJAP flag and SCAP control.

subfiles.title: End of the Petroleum Distribution Kodan
subfiles.about: Transmits a press release announcing restoration of petroleum distribution to private enterprise.
subfiles.summary: The Kodan ended on April 1, 1949; private Japanese and foreign companies took over distribution and sales.

subfiles.title: Petroleum situation in the Far East, follow-up
subfiles.about: Records Asiatic Petroleum's concerns after private distribution resumed in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Read describes unprofitable controlled prices, storage pooling, taxes and possible refinery reopening. Duncan notes the approaching expiry of Kosco's Korean contract.

subfiles.title: Petroleum refineries in Japan
subfiles.about: Records Henry Noel's case for rehabilitating Japanese refineries.
subfiles.summary: Noel estimates large savings from refining imported crude in Japan and advocates limited consolidation. He describes company partnerships, technical needs, Japanese frustration with restrictions and disagreement over the security risk.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding refinery discussion
subfiles.about: Supports Japanese refinery rehabilitation and requests a copy of the refinery report.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth doubts domestic refining would create a security risk.

subfiles.title: Excerpts on petroleum refineries in Japan
subfiles.about: Extracts Noel's estimates and arguments for reopening Japanese refineries.
subfiles.summary: The excerpts cover costs, savings, consolidation, commercial partnerships and Japanese impatience with occupation restrictions.

subfiles.title: British conditional approval for tanker calls
subfiles.about: Approves unaccompanied Japanese tanker calls at British ports subject to conditions.
subfiles.summary: Britain specifies flags, anchoring, crew confinement and compliance with port rules.

subfiles.title: Forwarding British tanker conditions
subfiles.about: Forwards British conditions for Japanese tanker calls without Allied representatives.
subfiles.summary: Moseley asks that SCAP receive the note and flag instructions.

subfiles.title: Army reply on Japanese refinery rehabilitation
subfiles.about: Describes planned crude imports and potential savings from Japanese refinery rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: West encloses the requested report and says SCAP is reviewing the program.

subfiles.title: Purchase of petroleum in Japan for sterling
subfiles.about: Records an Army inquiry about buying Japanese petroleum supplies with sterling.
subfiles.summary: McBride reserves judgment pending fuller facts on the sterling proposal.

subfiles.title: Forwarding refinery directive and information bulletin
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAPIN 2027 and a bulletin on Japan's petroleum industry.
subfiles.summary: The despatch highlights possible dollar savings and consolidation of Pacific refineries.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 2027: Pacific coast refineries and crude imports
subfiles.about: Rescinds refinery restrictions and permits approved rehabilitation and crude imports.
subfiles.summary: Owners must submit detailed plans; new refineries are excluded and imported crude proposals remain subject to SCAP review.

subfiles.title: The Petroleum Industry of Japan
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Summarizes Noel's report on Japanese refinery capacity and efficient reopening.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin estimates substantial savings from refining imported crude and recommends concentrating production in a few Pacific refineries. It continues beyond this section.
